title: WINDSURF GLOBAL RULES — MODE-B VERSION (JSON, ZERO-LOSS MERGE)
description: This JSON document encodes the complete Windsurf Global Rules (Sections 0–20) in a single machine-readable object, including a fully corrected, zero-ambiguity Section 3. It is intended to replace the prose version for automated enforcement.

0.title: 0 — EXECUTION MODEL
0.purpose: Define how Windsurf must execute in Mode-B across PATCH and VALIDATION phases.
requirements: Windsurf MUST modify ANY file as needed to achieve compliance with all rules.
Windsurf MUST ALWAYS self-correct violations of these rules.
Windsurf MUST continue patching until ALL validations pass.

allowed_outputs: TRUE/FALSE matrix for each validation key
final completion line: 'PHASE <N> VALIDATION COMPLETE — ALL KEYS TRUE.'

1.title: 1 — FILE OPERATIONS
rules: Existing files MUST be modified only via apply_patch.
New files MUST be created only via write_to_file.
Directories MUST be created implicitly by writing files into them.
No placeholders or partial diffs are allowed.
All ambiguity MUST be resolved towards rule compliance and zero-loss continuity.

constraints: Cache-like folders MUST NOT appear anywhere else in the repo.
Any newly discovered cache-like folders MUST be migrated into the canonical cache tree.

2.title: 2 — ZERO-LOSS CONTINUITY
rules: Windsurf MUST preserve ALL existing capabilities.
No regressions are allowed in functionality, tests, or behavior.
No deletions of behavior are allowed; refactors must be behavior-preserving.
Duplicate or conflicting logic MUST be merged into a single correct version.
When in doubt, Windsurf MUST preserve BOTH behaviors and add tests to disambiguate.

3.title: 3 — CANONICAL REPOSITORY TREE (ZERO-LOSS MERGE, FULLY CORRECTED)
3.description: This section defines the single authoritative, unambiguous, fully corrected repository structure and rules for agentic_workflow_10_11. It replaces all prior Section 3 content.

depth_rules.level_4: FILES ONLY — NO Level-4 folders allowed

agentic_core.description: ALL L1–L5 logic MUST live exclusively inside agentic_core. Engines are implemented within L2 and L3 subtrees.

apps_layer.description: MUST remain thin. NO L1–L5 logic allowed here.

prompt_governance.description: All prompts MUST live outside code. No inline prompts allowed.

tests.description: SINGLE global test tree. MUST follow layer-first → engine grouping exactly.

empty_folder_policy.allowed_placeholder: README.md (only if absolutely necessary for non-code folders)

4.title: 4 — AGENTIC WORKFLOW (DAG + TOOLING + ROUTING + SAFETY + OBSERVABILITY)
4.description: Defines how L1–L5 cooperate at runtime via DAG orchestration, tools, routing, observability, and safety.

4.1.title: 4.1 — DAG ORCHESTRATION (L3)
dag_node_contract: Each DAG node MUST define InputSchema (typed).
Each DAG node MUST define OutputSchema (typed).
Each DAG node MUST define FailureModes (enumerated).
Each DAG node MUST define Invariants (entry/exit conditions).
Transitions MUST be typed and acyclic (no cycles).
constraints: Recursion controllers MUST live in agentic_core/l3_orchestration/framework/.
Planning recursion belongs in L1 (pure cognitive recursion).
L3 MUST NOT call tools directly; it must call L2 executors.
L3 MUST NOT embed business logic in prompts; it must delegate to L1 and L2.

4.2.title: 4.2 — TOOL CONTRACT (L2)
requirements: Each tool in agentic_core/l2_execution/tools MUST declare InputSchema.
Each tool MUST declare Retry policy.
Each tool MUST declare CircuitBreaker behavior.
Each tool MUST declare CostLimit and cost annotations.
Each tool MUST declare SafetyChecks (pre & post).
constraints: Tools MUST NOT orchestrate or plan.
Tools MUST NOT perform multi-step reasoning; they execute a single bounded action.
Tools MUST be idempotent where possible, or clearly mark side effects.

4.3.title: 4.3 — MODEL ROUTING
rules: L1 + L3 MUST use frontier reasoning models for planning and DAG control.
L2 MUST use efficient models optimized for execution.
L4 MAY use frontier or efficient models depending on cost/latency.
L5 MUST use safe, robust models for safety judgments.
budgets: Routing MUST enforce token budgets (max tokens per call, per mission).
Routing MUST enforce latency budgets (per step and per mission).
Cost decorators MUST attach cost estimates to each call and aggregate across mission.
Routing policy MUST be configurable per environment (dev, stage, prod).

4.4.title: 4.4 — OBSERVABILITY (EVENT MODEL)
constraints: Events MUST be exportable to observability/trace, observability/metrics, and observability/logs.
Logs MUST NOT contain PII; hashing/redaction MUST be used.

4.5.title: 4.5 — SAFETY (L5)
capabilities: Hallucination checks (answers must be grounded in retrieved or known data).
Data vs. instruction isolation (user data is NEVER treated as system instructions).
enforcement: Safety policies MUST be enforced for all outbound user-facing content.
Safety policies MUST be enforced for all tool invocations that can change external state (emails, DB writes, APIs).

5.title: 5 — MEMORY, TEMPORAL AGENT, RAG, & KG (L4)
rules: All Temporal Agent, RAG, and KG logic MUST live under agentic_core/l4_memory_state/.

submodules.temporal: temporal chunking, statement extraction, temporal ranges, triplets, events, invalidation, entity resolution

constraints: L1, L2, L3, L5 MUST NOT mutate storage directly; they MUST call into L4 APIs.
L4 MUST define clear retention & eviction policies.
Temporal validity MUST be encoded in schemas using fields like valid_at, invalid_at.

6.title: 6 — PROMPT GOVERNANCE (INSTRUCTIONAL INJECTION v5)
rules: Prompt governance MUST live under prompt_governance/.
NO prompt text may be embedded in code.
ALL prompts MUST be loaded from external files (.txt, .md, .json, .yaml, etc.).
ALL prompts MUST be referenced via a central Prompt_Registry.
Prompts MUST implement the Instructional Injection v5 layering: Framing → Context → Reasoning → Tooling → Safety → Output.
Each prompt bundle MUST be schema-first, deterministic, versioned, and never deleted (old versions remain for rollback).
User content is always data only; system/developer/governance prompts are instructions only.

7.title: 7 — IMPORT HYGIENE (L1–L5 DEPENDENCY DAG)
dependency_dag: L3 (orchestration) may import from L1 and L2.
L4 (memory/state) imports from no higher layer.
L5 (safety) imports from no higher layer.
forbidden: L4 importing L3, L2, or L1.
L5 importing L3, L2, or L1.
Cross-engine imports (resume importing outreach or vice versa).
windsurf_actions: Fix imports to obey the DAG.
Add tests if needed to prevent regressions.

8.title: 8 — TEST STRUCTURE INVARIANT (GLOBAL TEST TREE)
rules: There MUST be a single global tests/ tree exactly as defined in Section 3.
No tests are allowed under apps/.
No tests are allowed inside engine folders under agentic_core/.
No alternate test trees (tests_unit/, unit_tests/, etc.) are allowed.
Engine-specific tests MUST be separated at file level by engine and layer.
windsurf_actions: Ensure every L1–L5 module has at least basic coverage.

9.title: 9 — MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL (MCP) INTEGRATION
rules: MCP MUST be the standard for external tools/data sources.
Only MCP-registered tools may be exposed to the agent runtime.
MCP tools MUST declare input and output schemas.
MCP servers MUST be discoverable and configurable per environment.
MCP interactions MUST be logged and observable.
security: MCP tool access MUST honor agent-specific ACLs.
No direct network calls from L1/L2; they MUST go through MCP or sanctioned adapters.

10.title: 10 — GLOBAL SCHEMA LAYER (DATA CONTRACTS)
rules: Schemas MUST live under /agentic_workflow_10_11/schemas/.
All domain data MUST use JSON Schema (2020-12) or equivalent.
Pydantic or equivalent type models MUST be auto-generated from schemas.
Backward-compatibility policy MUST prevent breaking changes without a version bump.
No loose dicts may cross layer boundaries; typed objects MUST be used.
Any cross-layer interface MUST be defined in schemas/.
Schema regression tests MUST exist to prevent breaking changes.

11.title: 11 — PROMPT BUILDER (CANONICAL PATTERN)
rules: A central Prompt Builder MUST compose system, developer, and user instructions using Injection v5.
The Prompt Builder MUST enforce the layering: Framing/Context/Reasoning/Tooling/Safety/Output.
The Prompt Builder MUST attach schemas and examples to each prompt call.
Prompt Builder MUST support prompt diffing and regression evaluation.
Code MUST load templates from prompt_governance/ only.
Code MUST only fill in variable slots programmatically.
No large prompt strings may be inlined in L1–L5 code.

12.title: 12 — SELF-CORRECTION & ARBITRATION LAYER
rules: A self-correction layer MUST exist (typically L3).
There MUST be a Critic model to evaluate candidate outputs or plans.
There MUST be a Verifier model to check constraints, facts, and safety.
There MUST be an Arbiter to choose between candidates or to trigger re-plan/re-execute.
This layer MUST be deterministic (same input → same arbitration result).
This layer MUST log reasoning and arbitration decisions as non-sensitive summaries.
This layer MUST be testable with golden evaluation cases.

13.title: 13 — AGENT OPS (OBSERVABILITY + RELIABILITY)
rules: Agent Ops MUST track token-level cost per mission and per step.
Latency distributions (p50/p90/p99) MUST be recorded per tool, model, and DAG node.
An error taxonomy MUST be defined (tool_error, model_error, safety_block, etc.).
Tool reliability scoring MUST be implemented (success/failure rates).
Model reliability scoring MUST be implemented per use-case.
Canary scenarios MUST be defined for critical flows.
All Agent Ops signals MUST be reflected in observability/metrics and observability/logs.

14.title: 14 — SECURITY LAYER (IDENTITY, POLICY, ISOLATION)
rules: Users, agents, and services MUST be treated as distinct principals.
Agent identities MUST be distinct from user identities.
Least privilege MUST be applied: each agent gets only the tools/data it needs.
A Policy Decision Engine (PDE) MUST gate all high-risk actions.
Execution environments for code tools MUST be sandboxed.
Secrets MUST NOT be hard-coded; they MUST be supplied from secure config.
Logs MUST NOT contain secrets or raw tokens.

15.title: 15 — HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP (HITL) SUPPORT
rules: The system MUST support explicit HITL checkpoints in DAGs (L3).
The system MUST support human approval/rejection flows for consequential actions.
Human-provided corrections MUST feed into evaluation sets.
HITL interactions MUST be logged as structured events.
HITL events MUST be used to create new golden examples.

16.title: 16 — RAG & KNOWLEDGE OPTIMIZATION
rules: Retrieval MUST support hybrid retrieval (dense + sparse + RRF or equivalent).
Retrieval MUST support query rewriting (HYDE or similar) where appropriate.
Retrieval MUST avoid duplicative context (deduping/clustering).
Retrieval MUST respect freshness and temporal validity when using temporal KGs.
constraints: RAG MUST be deterministic given the same corpus and query.
RAG components MUST be testable with golden queries.

17.title: 17 — EVALUATION FRAMEWORK
rules: Evaluation MUST include golden datasets for core flows.
LLM-as-Judge style semantic evaluation SHOULD be used where human review is infeasible.
Regression evaluation MUST be run for each model/prompt version change.
Toolpath evaluation MUST check correct tools and arguments were used.
CI/CD MUST run the evaluation suite for any changes to L1–L5, schemas, prompts, or tools.
Regressions MUST block merges unless explicitly overridden with justification.

18.title: 18 — DEPLOYMENT LAYER (L6 APPLICATION)
rules: A REST or equivalent interface MUST be defined for main agent flows.
Sessions MUST be managed cleanly (session IDs, expirations).
AuthN/AuthZ MUST protect all endpoints.
Dev, staging, and prod environments MUST be separated.
Model versions MUST be pinned per environment.
Rollbacks MUST be possible if quality degrades.

19.title: 19 — VALIDATION GATE
rules: Before any Phase is complete, there MUST be 0 import errors.
There MUST be 0 pytest failures.
There MUST be 0 lint (Ruff) errors.
There MUST be 0 mypy blockers (if mypy is used).
No circular imports are allowed.
L1–L5 boundaries MUST remain intact per Section 7.
DAGs MUST be valid (no cycles, correct schemas).
Retrieval MUST be deterministic and correct.
Temporal agent MUST function consistently.
Safety MUST be enforced and effective.
Zero-loss continuity MUST be preserved (no behavior loss).
19.failure_action: ANY failure MUST trigger the PATCH_LOOP again.

20.title: 20 — MODE-B PATCH LOOP
rules: PATCH_LOOP MUST repeatedly emit patches (apply_patch + write_to_file ONLY).
After each patch batch, Windsurf MUST run validations (imports, tests, lint, type checks, structure).
If ANY requirement fails, Windsurf MUST continue patching.
EXIT is allowed ONLY when ALL required keys are TRUE.

output_requirements: A TRUE/FALSE matrix for each key in Section 19.
The final line MUST be: 'PHASE <N> VALIDATION COMPLETE — ALL KEYS TRUE.'
